articles.title: Drones atingem navios no Mar Negro e afundam embarcação perto da Bulgária; 11 estão desaparecidos | G1
articles.standfirst: Primeiro-ministro búlgaro classificou ataque como "absolutamente inaceitável"; país busca apoio da Otan e da União Europeia.
articles.summary: Primeiro-ministro búlgaro classificou ataque como "absolutamente inaceitável"; país busca apoio da Otan e da União Europeia.
articles.body:
Veículos policiais em uma área enquanto tripulantes resgatados de um navio danificado em um ataque de drone são levados em ambulâncias em Varna. — Foto: Bulphoto Agency

Drones atingiram dois navios no Mar Negro, próximo à costa da Bulgária, nesta terça-feira (13), afundando uma das embarcações e desencadeando operações de resgate de emergência, informou o primeiro-ministro búlgaro, Rumen Radev.

As equipes de resgate retiraram os 15 tripulantes de um dos navios , o Chelsea 3, de bandeira maltesa. Cinco deles receberam atendimento por ferimentos leves, disse Radev em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais.

A tripulação, composta por sete cidadãos ucranianos e oito cidadãos do Azerbaijão, relatou que o convés e o casco do navio foram atingidos por três drones aéreos.

Radev acrescentou que um tripulante da embarcação que afundou foi resgatado, sem fornecer detalhes sobre os demais ocupantes. Onze pessoas estão desaparecidos, segundo uma autoridade regional.

"Segundo informações que recebemos do centro de resgate... cinco pessoas foram resgatadas e 11 estão desaparecidas. Esta é uma informação preliminar", disse a porta-voz da região nordeste de Dobrich.

Os ataques aos dois navios ocorreram a 29 e 27,5 quilômetros da costa búlgara.

Durante uma reunião de emergência do Conselho de Segurança da Bulgária nesta terça-feira, Radev classificou os ataques como "absolutamente inaceitáveis" e afirmou que o país busca auxílio da Otan e da União Europeia.

Embora as autoridades não tenham evidências claras sobre os responsáveis pelos ataques, "a lógica, como já afirmei, indica que o resultado favorece a Federação Russa", disse Radev.

Em uma publicação na rede social X nesta terça-feira, o ministro das Relações Exteriores da Ucrânia, Andrii Sybiha, atribuiu a responsabilidade pelos ataques à Rússia.

"O mais recente ataque da Rússia contra embarcações comerciais perto das águas territoriais da Bulgária, que feriu cidadãos ucranianos e azerbaijanos, demonstra mais uma vez o desprezo deliberado de Moscou pelas vidas civis e pela segurança marítima no Mar Negro", escreveu Sybiha.

Ele afirmou que a Ucrânia está pedindo a seus parceiros que aumentem a pressão sobre a Rússia, reforcem as sanções e tomem medidas decisivas para responsabilizar Moscou e proteger a liberdade de navegação.

"O Mar Negro é uma linha vital para a segurança alimentar global. A Rússia o está atacando para usar a fome como arma e manter o mundo como refém. Isso deve ser enfrentado com firmeza", escreveu o chanceler.

A presidente da Comissão Europeia, Ursula von der Leyen, também condenou duramente os incidentes e afirmou que o Mar Negro "se tornou mais uma frente de escalada" na guerra da Rússia contra a Ucrânia.

"Isso é inaceitável. Condeno veementemente os ataques de drones contra navios mercantes perto da costa da Bulgária. Eles colocam em grave risco a vida das tripulações e ameaçam a segurança no Mar Negro", escreveu ela no X.

"Estamos ao lado da Bulgária e agradecemos aos socorristas pela rápida resposta. Os responsáveis devem ser responsabilizados."

Os ataques ocorreram exatamente uma semana depois de drones marítimos e aéreos atingirem outras duas embarcações comerciais na zona econômica exclusiva da Bulgária no Mar Negro. Um navio de bandeira do Togo afundou, enquanto uma balsa búlgara retirou os 18 tripulantes de uma embarcação de bandeira de Palau.

Segundo o presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky, as Forças Armadas da Ucrânia não realizaram operações próximas aos locais dos ataques da semana passada. O líder ucraniano atribuiu a responsabilidade à Rússia.

Um dia antes, um cargueiro de propriedade turca que transportava milho pegou fogo após um ataque de drones e posteriormente afundou no Mar Negro, próximo à costa da Romênia. Duas pessoas morreram e 11 tripulantes foram resgatados, segundo autoridades romenas.

A Rússia não comentou imediatamente o incidente desta terça-feira.

Radev disse que convocaria a embaixadora da Rússia na Bulgária, Eleonora Mitrofanova, para uma conversa ainda nesta terça-feira.Drones atingem navios no Mar Negro e afundam embarcação perto da Bulgária

articles.title: Presidente da FIFA recebeu US$ 1,7 milhão sem declarar da Copa, diz TV | G1
articles.standfirst: Giani Infantino recebeu quantia da FWC2026, braço da FIFA criado para gerir a Copa do Mundo de 2026, segundo documentos da Receita dos EUA e da própria entidade aos que a ESPN teve acesso. Entidade negou irregularidades.
articles.summary: O presidente da FIFA, Gianni Infantino, recebeu um pagamento de US$ 1,72 milhão (cerca de R$ 8,6 milhões) de forma não declarada, segundo a ESPN com base na Receita dos EUA.
articles.body:
O presidente da Fifa, Gianni Infantino (à esquerda), e o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, na final da Copa do Mundo de 2026. — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

O presidente da FIFA, Gianni Infantino, recebeu um pagamento de US$ 1,72 milhão (cerca de R$ 8,6 milhões) relacionado à Copa do Mundo e de forma não declarada, segundo documentos da FIFA e da Receita Federal dos Estados Unidos obtidos pela rede de TV ESPN.

De acordo com reportagem da ESPN publicada nesta terça-feira (13), a transação representa uma possível violação dos estatutos da FIFA , por conta da suposta falta de transparência. A denúncia foi feita em um momento em que Infantino enfrenta uma onda de críticas e pedidos para que deixo o cargo ( leia mais abaixo ).

👉 Infantino, diz a reportagem, recebeu o pagamento em 2024 da FWC2026, a organização oficial da FIFA criada para gerir e operar a Copa do Mundo de 2026. A FWC2026 é sediada nos Estados Unidos.

O valor de US$ 1,72 milhão somou-se ao salário e aos benefícios que Infantino recebeu da FIFA em 2024, totalizando cerca de US$ 4,9 milhões (cerca de R$ 24,5 milhões). Essa remuneração adicional não constou no relatório anual da FIFA de 2024, segundo a reportagem.

Conforme os próprios estatutos da FIFA, "a remuneração individual do presidente da FIFA, dos membros do Conselho e do secretário-geral da FIFA deve ser tornada pública".

Infantino no 50º Congresso Ordinário da UEFA, em 12 de fevereiro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

Um porta-voz da FIFA disse à ESPN que a organização "rejeita veementemente qualquer sugestão de que tenha havido violação" dos estatutos.

"A FIFA não paga um segundo salário ao presidente da FIFA e cumpre todas as exigências de divulgação de informações relativas à remuneração", afirmou a entidade em comunicado.

"A FIFA rejeita veementemente quaisquer alegações de que tenha deixado de divulgar informações financeiras ou violado os estatutos da entidade. As contas da FIFA passam por auditoria independente, e todas as declarações estão em conformidade com as regulamentações fiscais da Suíça, dos Estados Unidos e de outras jurisdições", disse ainda a entidade.

👉 A suposta verba extra é a mais recente polêmica envolvendo Infantino, de 56 anos, que ocupa o cargo desde 2016. No início deste ano, o dirigente foi alvo de críticas devido a um plano — posteriormente abandonado — de vender uma participação de 20% na Copa do Mundo a investidores privados.

articles.title: Jacaré é encontrado dentro de casa e resgatado no Acre; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal foi encontrado em uma residência no bairro Alberto Castro, em Brasiléia, na manhã dessa segunda-feira (12). Após o resgate, ele foi solto às margens do rio Acre.
articles.summary: Animal foi encontrado em uma residência no bairro Alberto Castro, em Brasiléia, na manhã dessa segunda-feira (12). Após o resgate, ele foi solto às margens do rio Acre.
articles.body:
🏡🐊😱 Moradores do bairro Alberto Castro, em Brasiléia , no interior do Acre, levaram um susto na manhã desta segunda-feira (12). É que um jacaré foi encontrado na área externa de uma residência , em um espaço onde havia pedaços de canos de ferro. ( Veja vídeo acima )

O animal mobilizou uma equipe do 5º Batalhão de Proteção e Combate a Incêndios Florestais (5º BPCIF), do Corpo de Bombeiros Militar, que foi acionada para fazer o resgate.

Conforme o Corpo de Bombeiros, os militares capturaram o jacaré com o auxílio de uma alçapão, tomando os cuidados necessários para evitar acidentes e preservar o estado do animal.

Após o resgate, o réptil foi transportado e solto às margens do rio Acre, em uma área adequada para seu retorno à natureza.

Jacaré foi encontrado na área externa de uma casa em Brasiléia nessa segunda-feira (12) — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

Os bombeiros orientam que, ao encontrar um animal silvestre em uma área urbana, a população mantenha distância e não tente capturá-lo por conta própria.

⚠️A recomendação é acionar a corporação pelo telefone 193 para que os profissionais façam a retirada com segurança.

Após o resgate, jacaré foi solto às margens do rio Acre — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

A presença de jacarés faz parte dos ecossistemas amazônicos. Esses répteis vivem principalmente em rios, lagos, igarapés e áreas alagadas, ambientes que oferecem abrigo e alimento.

Na Amazônia, há diferentes espécies, entre elas o jacaré-tinga e o jacaré-açu, que se distinguem, entre outras características, pelo tamanho.

O jacaré-açu é a maior espécie de jacaré da América Latina e pode ultrapassar cinco metros de comprimento. Já o jacaré-tinga, também conhecido como jacaré-de-óculos, tem porte menor e apresenta ampla distribuição geográfica, segundo informações do Instituto Mamirauá.

Embora esses animais façam parte da fauna regional, encontrá-los dentro de residências não é uma situação que deva ser tratada como inofensiva.

A proximidade entre áreas urbanas e ambientes naturais pode favorecer encontros com animais silvestres. Além de integrarem a cadeia alimentar, os jacarés têm papel ecológico nos ambientes aquáticos.

articles.title: Drone attack sinks ship off Bulgaria coast, second strike in a week
articles.summary: A drone attack sank a ship off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast on Tuesday, while another vessel was also hit, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said.
articles.body: A drone attack sank a ship off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast on Tuesday, while another vessel was also hit, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said.According to Reuters, the Maltese-flagged vessel Chelsea 3, which is owned by a Ukrainian company, was struck by three drones about 18 nautical miles off Bulgaria’s coast. All 15 crew members aboard the ship were rescued, while the second vessel sank in the attack.Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said there was no clear evidence identifying those responsible for the attacks, describing the incident as the second of its kind in a week.“This is absolutely unacceptable — another attack in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters,” Radev said, adding that he would speak with Nato secretary-general Mark Rutte.In an earlier incident on October 6, drones struck two merchant ships in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea.The Togo-flagged cargo ship Alfa Watan sank, while the vessel Able, which was carrying grain, was damaged. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia for that attack.Russia denied involvement in the attack, with its embassy in Sofia saying the merchant vessel Alfa Watan was not among the targets hit by Russian drones. The Russian defence ministry said the origin of the drones would need to be established through an investigation.The attacks have raised concerns over the security of commercial vessels operating near Bulgaria, a member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (Nato).The Black Sea remains a crucial route for grain and other commodities, particularly for Ukraine, and repeated strikes on merchant ships could disrupt maritime trade and increase risks for shipping operators.You use AI every day. articles.title: Breaking Bad star RJ Mitte was treated for cerebral palsy as a child; he built an acting career and championed disability rights as his family foundation donated $117,000 to a Texas wellness programme
articles.summary: RJ Mitte, the actor best known for playing Walter White Jr., also known as Flynn, in Breaking Bad, died on October 12, 2026, at the age of 34.
articles.body: RJ Mitte, the actor best known for playing Walter White Jr., also known as Flynn, in Breaking Bad, died on October 12, 2026, at the age of 34. Diagnosed with cerebral palsy at the age of three, Mitte drew on his personal experiences to advocate for people with disabilities. Beyond his acting career, he supported organisations including Shriners Children's and United Cerebral Palsy, raising awareness about disability inclusion and bullying. His philanthropic connections also extended to the Roy F. and Joann Cole Mitte Foundation, which awarded $117,000 to the Brownsville Wellness Coalition's StartUp Texas Accelerator Program in 2024.RJ Mitte's childhood experience with cerebral palsyMitte was diagnosed with cerebral palsy when he was three years old. The neurological condition can affect movement, muscle tone, coordination and posture. During his childhood, he received treatment at Shriners Hospitals for Children in Shreveport, Louisiana, where specialists used casting and physical therapy to address difficulties with his walking.His experience later shaped his public advocacy. By speaking about his childhood and the challenges associated with the condition, he helped raise awareness of the importance of specialist healthcare and greater opportunities for children with disabilities.From Walter White Jr. to a successful acting careerMitte rose to international recognition through Breaking Bad, the crime drama starring Bryan Cranston as Walter White. He played Walter's son, Walter White Jr., throughout the show's five seasons, which aired from 2008 to 2013.The character also has cerebral palsy, creating a personal connection between Mitte and the role. His performance brought a disabled character to mainstream television while portraying him as a teenager with his own personality, relationships and family struggles.Following the series, Mitte continued working in television and film. His credits included Switched at Birth, The Guardians of Justice and Triumph, a 2021 film in which he played a high-school wrestler with cerebral palsy. He also pursued modelling and advocated for greater opportunities for disabled performers.RJ Mitte became an ambassador for the hospital that treated himIn February 2014, Shriners Hospitals for Children named Mitte a national ambassador for its Love to the rescue campaign. Having received treatment at the hospital as a child, he returned to support its work by sharing his experiences through public-service announcements and appearances.The campaign aimed to raise awareness of the specialist care available to children and encourage public donations to support the hospital's work. Mitte's involvement helped connect his personal experience with the needs of other children and their families.Campaigning against bullyingMitte also worked with Shriners on its Cut the Bull anti-bullying campaign, which encouraged people to look beyond physical differences and disabilities. The initiative addressed the bullying and social exclusion that children with disabilities can experience.Having spoken publicly about his own experiences with bullying, Mitte used his platform to promote understanding and acceptance. His involvement highlighted the importance of creating environments where children are treated with respect regardless of their physical condition.His work with United Cerebral PalsyMitte supported United Cerebral Palsy, an organisation that advocates for people with cerebral palsy and other disabilities. He served as an ambassador and participated in fundraising activities associated with the organisation, including events linked to its San Diego chapter.His advocacy extended beyond healthcare to employment and representation. He spoke about the barriers disabled people face in professional settings and the need for greater access to opportunities across different industries.Mitte used his experience in Hollywood to call for better representation of people with disabilities in film, television and modelling. He advocated for disabled performers to receive more opportunities to audition for roles and portray characters whose lives were not defined solely by their conditions.His work included involvement in initiatives associated with the Screen Actors Guild and the Inclusion in the Arts and Media of Performers with Disabilities initiative. He also worked with the National Disability Institute's Real Economic Impact Tour, which focused on improving economic inclusion for people with disabilities.Through these efforts, Mitte highlighted the importance of equal opportunities in employment and entertainment, as well as more authentic portrayals of disabled people on screen.Mitte Foundation awarded $117,000 to a Texas wellness programmeThe Roy F. and Joann Cole Mitte Foundation, a family philanthropic organisation, awarded $117,000 to the Brownsville Wellness Coalition in 2024 to support its StartUp Texas Accelerator Program, according to the foundation's published grant records.The foundation also awarded $135,000 to the Valley Zoological Society for a conservation cabin at Gladys Porter Zoo and $100,000 to the Mitte Cultural District to support its executive director position and related development and office expenses.The foundation supports a range of community initiatives, including education, scholarships, healthcare and services for people with physical and intellectual disabilities. Its charitable activities provide a broader picture of the family's philanthropic involvement alongside Mitte's public advocacy.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: South Korea tests hypersonic missile: A new threat to North Korea's underground bunkers?
articles.summary: South Korea has successfully tested a domestically developed hypersonic boost-glide vehicle, with footage showing the vehicle impacting the water at the
articles.body: South Korea has successfully tested a domestically developed hypersonic boost-glide vehicle, with footage showing the vehicle impacting the water at the end of its flight. The missile has been tested by South Korea's Agency for Defense Development (ADD). The weapon would give Seoul a significant new way to hold targets in North Korea at risk as the arms race on the peninsula deepens. It follows the Hyunmoo-5, whose massive unitary warhead already lets South Korea threaten deeply buried and hardened targets, and fits the country's Korea Massive Punishment and Retaliation policy.At the very high speeds reached in the terminal phase, boost-glide vehicles also offer bunker-busting benefits. South Korea is also developing an air-breathing hypersonic cruise missile and new air- and sea-launched ballistic missiles for its warships and submarines. It remains to be seen when an operational capability will be fielded. Beyond North Korea, China and Russia have also been growing concerns for Seoul.Hypersonic weapons travel above Mach 5, or about 6,100 km an hour, and fall into two categories. Glide vehicles are boosted by rockets to high altitude and some of these weapons are designed to manoeuvring unpredictably while gliding to their target. Cruise missiles are powered by engines such as scramjets and fly at sustained hypersonic speeds within the atmosphere. Unlike ballistic missiles, which follow predictable arcs, both can change course mid-flight and fly low to exploit the radar horizon.Operation Sindoor showed how hard even a supersonic weapon is to stop. A missile at nearly Mach 3 flying low would be detected by ground radar at around 15 km, giving about 15 seconds to impact. At Mach 5, the same distance is covered in under nine seconds, and since most surface-to-air missiles fly below Mach 5, few systems could intercept such a weapon.Building these systems is hard, hypersonic vehicles face extreme heat and need advanced cooling, scramjet combustion is difficult to sustain, and the plasma sheath around the vehicle disrupts guidance and communications. Materials must also withstand huge stress, flying fast at low altitude demands extra power, and test facilities are scarce and costly.India's projects include the Hypersonic Technology Demonstrator Vehicle, which reached Mach 6, the planned BrahMos-II at around Mach 7, the Dhvani glide vehicle, the Long Range Anti-Ship Missile (LR-AShM) for attacking ships including carriers and the Extended Trajectory-Long Duration Hypersonic Cruise Missile (ET-LDHCM).Elsewhere, the US is pursuing the AGM-183 air-launched weapon, the scramjet-powered Hypersonic Air-breathing Weapon Concept (HAWC) and the US Navy's Conventional Prompt Strike missile. China has fielded the DF-17 with the DF-ZF glide vehicle, capable of Mach 5 to 10, and tested an orbital system in 2021. Russia has combat-tested the Mach 10 Kinzhal in Ukraine and fields the ship-launched Tsirkon at Mach 8. France is developing the V-MaX, Australia is working with the US on the Southern Cross experiment, and Japan is building a glide projectile for island defence, with deployment planned by 2030.

articles.title: Beyonce marked her 45th birthday with a $2 million gift to the Studio Museum in Harlem; it has championed Black artists since 1968 and recently opened a new home
articles.summary: Beyonce marked her 45th birthday on September 4, 2026, with a $2 million gift to the Studio Museum in Harlem, supporting an institution dedicated to
articles.body: Beyonce marked her 45th birthday on September 4, 2026, with a $2 million gift to the Studio Museum in Harlem, supporting an institution dedicated to artists of African descent and the exploration of Black culture through art. Announced by her company, Parkwood Entertainment, the donation reflected her interest in art collecting and her appreciation for the museum's exhibitions, which introduced her to emerging Black artists whose work she admired. The gift came less than a year after the institution opened its purpose-built home in Harlem in November 2025. Founded in 1968, the museum continues to support artists through exhibitions, educational initiatives and professional development programmes.Beyonce's gift and her connection to the museumIn her birthday announcement, Beyonce highlighted the role art plays in telling stories about the past and present, while noting that it is not always accessible to everyone. She praised the museum for its connection with the community and credited its exhibitions with introducing her to young and emerging Black artists. Thelma Golden, the museum's director and chief curator, thanked the singer for recognising the institution's contribution to Harlem, New York and audiences worldwide. Golden said the gift would help strengthen the museum's work with those communities. Beyonce's interest in the institution connects her personal passion for collecting art with its mission to make the work of artists of African descent more visible.A museum founded to champion Black artistsThe Studio Museum in Harlem was founded in 1968 by artists, community activists and philanthropists seeking to create greater opportunities for artists of African descent. At a time when their work was underrepresented in many major cultural institutions, the museum established a dedicated space for exhibitions, discussion and the preservation of Black artistic expression. Over the decades, it has developed an internationally recognised programme of exhibitions, public events and educational activities. Its permanent collection contains nearly 9,000 artworks, documenting artistic contributions by artists of African descent from the 19th century to the present.The museum also connects artists with audiences and provides opportunities for professional development, helping emerging and established practitioners develop their work and reach wider audiences.Its artist-in-residence programme supports emerging talentThe museum launched its Artist-in-Residence programme in 1969. Since then, it has supported more than 150 artists of African and Afro-Latinx descent, providing resources to develop their practices and establish professional connections. Three artists are selected annually for an 11-month residency. Participants receive studio space, a stipend, research support and professional development opportunities. Their work is presented in a culminating exhibition accompanied by a publication.The 2026 cohort comprised Derriann Pharr, Simonette Quamina and Taylor Simmons. They became the first residents to work in the museum's new building, with their residency running from March through October 2026. The programme reflects the museum's commitment to supporting artists beyond exhibition opportunities by providing the time, resources and institutional support needed to develop their work.The museum opened a new home in HarlemOn November 15, 2025, the museum opened its new seven-storey building at its longtime location on West 125th Street in Harlem. The 82,000-square-foot facility was designed by Adjaye Associates, with Cooper Robertson serving as executive architect. The building includes exhibition galleries, educational facilities, flexible public spaces and a dedicated artist-in-residence centre. It more than doubled the space available for exhibitions and the residency programme while expanding areas for public engagement.The redevelopment followed a seven-year process and was supported by a fundraising campaign that had raised more than $300 million by the opening. New York State reported a project cost of $160 million and combined state investment of $10.9 million. The new building gives the museum greater capacity to host exhibitions, deliver educational programmes and support artists while maintaining its longstanding presence in Harlem.What Beyonce's gift means for the institutionThe $2 million contribution was announced as a gift to the museum, without specifying a particular exhibition, artwork acquisition or programme to receive the entire amount. The institution's wider activities include maintaining its permanent collection, organising exhibitions, supporting artists through residencies and providing educational opportunities. Its expanded facilities offer additional space for these initiatives. Beyonce's statement established a direct connection between her support and the museum's work, particularly its role in introducing her to emerging artists. Her contribution also draws attention to the importance of institutions that provide visibility and professional opportunities for artists whose work has historically been underrepresented.A birthday gift with a cultural connectionBeyonce's $2 million gift combines her interest in art collecting with support for an institution that has championed artists of African descent for nearly six decades. The timing, following the museum's move into its new Harlem home, places the contribution within a significant period in its history. The donation supports an organisation whose work extends beyond exhibitions to artist development, education and the preservation of Black artistic expression. It also highlights the role that cultural institutions can play in helping emerging artists reach new audiences and build sustainable careers.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: ‘I have not been transferred’: Tukaram Mundhe denies rumours, vows to continue Maharashtra FDA crackdown
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) commissioner Tukaram Mundhe on Monday denied speculation about his transfer, saying he continues to
articles.body: MUMBAI: Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) commissioner Tukaram Mundhe on Monday denied speculation about his transfer, saying he continues to head the department and its enforcement drive against unsafe food, adulterated products and substandard medicines will go on.The clarification came amid buzz about a possible transfer of the senior IAS officer, who has seen frequent transfers during his administrative career.The speculation gained traction after the state government named Mundhe secretary of a five-member committee set up to probe alleged paper leaks and irregularities in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) examinations."No, I have not been transferred from FDA," Mundhe said in a post on X on Monday night."I continue to serve as Commissioner, FDA Maharashtra. Our fight against unsafe, substandard, adulterated food and spurious, substandard drugs goes on," he added.Tukaram Mundhe’s FDA crackdown draws public attentionMundhe’s tenure as FDA commissioner has attracted considerable attention, with consumers welcoming the department’s intensified action against food safety violations, even as sections of the restaurant and food business industry have opposed measures taken against their establishments.The FDA has stepped up inspections, raids and enforcement action against eateries and food businesses over alleged violations, including the sale or use of unsafe and adulterated products.It has also acted against establishments over licensing and compliance issues as part of its effort to enforce food safety regulations.While consumers have appreciated the emphasis on accountability and food safety, some restaurant operators have resisted the action. Certain enforcement measures have also been challenged in courts, bringing aspects of the FDA’s regulatory drive under legal scrutiny.The enforcement campaign has kept Mundhe’s tenure in the spotlight, with food safety compliance and the functioning of eateries receiving greater public attention.Mundhe appointed secretary of MPSC paper leak inquiry panelMundhe’s appointment to the committee probing alleged paper leaks in MPSC examinations followed protests over the functioning of the state recruitment body.Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said last week that the five-member committee would examine the tenures of current and former chairpersons and members of the MPSC.The panel has been tasked with investigating allegations of paper leaks and irregularities in examinations conducted by the commission.(With PTI inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: In 2005, two Ohio brothers bought a flooded quarry for $330,000 and spent 15 years improving it; 21 years later, the village abandoned its bid to seize the 72.5-acre site and now has a $206,000 judgment lien against it
articles.summary: Two brothers in Ohio who bought an abandoned, flooded quarry for $330,000 in 2005 and spent 15 years improving it have been caught in a long legal dispute
articles.body: Two brothers in Ohio who bought an abandoned, flooded quarry for $330,000 in 2005 and spent 15 years improving it have been caught in a long legal dispute with the village where the property is located. Steve and Tim Snyder had planned to sell the land in 2021, but the Village of Luckey began proceedings to acquire it through eminent domain, a legal power that allows governments to take private property for public use with compensation.The dispute continued for nearly five years before the village abandoned its attempt to acquire the property in April this year. However, the legal battle has left Luckey facing approximately $206,000 in legal fees, with a judgment lien now recorded against the village.According to a report by The Blade, the amount represents nearly one-third of the village's general fund balance of approximately $640,000 at the end of 2025. The payment has not yet been made because the property owners are challenging the settlement agreement reached by their former lawyer.The case began with a failed property auction in September 2021. The brothers alleged that village officials had discouraged potential buyers from bidding, while Luckey maintained that it wanted the quarry as a possible public water source. The disagreement eventually reached the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, where the brothers' federal constitutional claims were dismissed.15 years of improving quarrySteve and Tim Snyder purchased the inactive quarry and surrounding land in March 2005 through their company, T&S Agriventures LLC. They paid $330,000 for the property, intending to improve it for future development or sale.Over the following 15 years, they worked on the land's topography and grading, cleared vegetation, established electricity and sanitary sewer services, and maintained the quarry lake. Their aim was to make the property suitable for residential or other development.In July 2021, the brothers hired Beth Rose Real Estate and Auctions LLC to market the property. An auction was scheduled for September 18, with a reserve price to prevent the land from selling below an agreed amount.However, after learning about the proposed sale, the Village of Luckey began considering acquiring the property itself. In August 2021, the village council unanimously authorised its attorney to begin the eminent domain process. Officials initially identified a public water supply or park as possible uses, before later specifying water supply alone.What happened at the auction?Days before the auction, village officials told the brothers that any purchase offer would depend on laboratory results assessing the quarry's water. They also indicated that the eminent domain process could take several years.On the auction day, the village placed temporary 'No parking; signs on nearby public streets. Its representatives attended the event but did not bid.The brothers alleged that the officials' presence discouraged buyers. After bidding closed at $610,000, the property remained unsold because the highest offer was below the reserve price.According to the court documents, the auction company later contacted registered bidders, several of whom said the village's actions had influenced their decision not to bid.The village continued pursuing the land and, in September 2022, offered the brothers $525,000. The dispute subsequently moved into court.Court rejected brothers' claimsThe Snyders and their auctioneer filed a federal lawsuit alleging violations of constitutional protections concerning private property, equal treatment and due process.In February 2024, a federal district court dismissed their claims. The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals subsequently upheld that decision.The majority ruled that the village's announcement of its intention to acquire the property did not itself amount to an unconstitutional taking. It noted that the brothers still owned the land and that the $610,000 auction bid demonstrated the property had not lost all economic value.However, Circuit Judge Eric Clay disagreed in a dissenting opinion. He argued that the brothers had presented sufficient allegations of deliberate interference with the auction to allow their takings claim to proceed.The majority also acknowledged concerns about aspects of the village's conduct but concluded that the allegations did not establish a constitutional violation.Village abandons acquisition but faces billLuckey continued its attempt to acquire the quarry until April 2026, when the village council formally abandoned the eminent domain proceedings.The decision led to a settlement involving legal fees, with a $206,000 judgment lien recorded against the village in the Wood County Court of Common Pleas.However, the settlement remains disputed. Steve Snyder alleged in court documents that the family's former attorney, Zachary Murry, agreed to the settlement in July without consulting them.The family is seeking to reverse the agreement because it prevents further claims against individual village officials and limits recovery to legal fees rather than additional damages.The village's payment was due on August 15, but Mayor Mike McNulty said officials were waiting for the court to resolve the dispute over the settlement.What legal bill mean for LuckeyLuckey, a village of approximately 1,000 residents, ended 2025 with $640,217 in its general fund, according to financial statements cited by The Blade. Its annual revenue was approximately $1.16 million.The potential legal payment is therefore a substantial expense for the village. Nevertheless, McNulty maintained that essential services, including streets, sewer operations and other everyday functions, were not at risk."The village is able to operate functionally," he told The Blade. "We're not going to be able to go and build a swimming pool or something like that. The everyday function of the village, streets, sewer, things like that- the village is fine."You use AI every day. articles.title: Nuclear sites fortified, loyalists rallied: Iran braces for possible US attacks after midterms
articles.summary: Iran has strengthened defences around sensitive nuclear sites and stepped up efforts to rally domestic support as it prepares for possible renewed US
articles.body: Iran has strengthened defences around sensitive nuclear sites and stepped up efforts to rally domestic support as it prepares for possible renewed US strikes after the November 3 midterm elections, the Wall Street Journal reported. Tehran has also warned regional officials that a fresh conflict could spill across the Gulf, with threats of land incursions into neighbouring countries and attacks on regional infrastructure, US forces and commercial shipping.The warnings, conveyed by Iranian officials in public statements and private conversations with regional counterparts, are part of Tehran’s effort to deter potential American attacks after the November 3 midterm elections.Some Iranian officials have hinted that Iranian forces could cross into neighbouring countries if Washington resumes strikes, people familiar with the warnings told the WSJ.Iran’s top national security official, Mohsen Rezaei, said on Sunday that Tehran could target the United Arab Emirates, as well as data centres and internet cables across the region.Tehran has separately warned Arab officials that it could strike regional targets, including Saudi oil facilities, if hostilities resume, according to people familiar with the discussions. Such threats would add to the security concerns facing Saudi Arabia, which has also come under attack from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels.Washington and Tehran have been in a prolonged military stand-off but Iran has steadily been rebuilding its capacity for further fighting rather than making concessions. Iran has limited ability to defend itself against advanced American fighter jets, high-altitude bombers and cruise missiles, giving it an incentive to threaten a broader regional conflict to raise the potential costs of a US attack.Iran threatens US personnel, shippingIran has also warned mediators that it could more aggressively target American personnel, including by attempting to sink US warships in the Middle East and kill their crews, the WSJ reported, citing people familiar with the warnings.Iranian missiles came close to American warships during attacks in September. The Pentagon moved a dozen B-1 bombers from a British military base last week amid concerns that Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps was planning a drone attack.Meanwhile, Iran has intensified attacks on vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz, at least three commercial vessels were hit over the weekend. A drone attack also set fire to the Emirati tanker Petro Dolphin near Oman on Sunday, leaving two Indian sailors missing.The US military is preparing for a possible resumption of hostilities. A third aircraft carrier strike group and another Marine expeditionary unit are heading towards the Middle East, while the Pentagon is considering deploying additional air-defence equipment and munitions to regional bases, the WSJ reported.US president Donald Trump has ruled out attacking Iran before the November 3 midterm elections, but has publicly considered striking the country’s Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site. US officials have also said the military is preparing options for further strikes.Iran has used the pause in direct fighting to rebuild missile and drone facilities and replenish its arsenal. Satellite imagery shows that it has also strengthened defences around sensitive sites, including the Pickaxe Mountain and Natanz nuclear facilities.Iranian officials have also said the country’s airports, seaports and power plants have prepared for wartime conditions by installing shelters and backup supplies.Alongside these preparations, Tehran has stepped up efforts to mobilise domestic support. State media has broadcast pro-government rallies, while billboards in the capital advertise civilian training courses in the use of shoulder-fired anti-aircraft missiles and sniper rifles. The Revolutionary Guard has also publicised the training of female commando units and sent personnel to a kindergarten in northeastern Iran to recount stories of the earlier fighting.You use AI every day. articles.body: A plump eastern diamondback rattlesnake turned a day of lawn work into a moment a Florida family will not forget. Paul Tremblay and his son Brandon stepped outside their Gulf Cove home in Charlotte County and found the venomous snake right in front of them. Their decision to call emergency officials rather than handle the animal offers a useful lesson for every Florida homeowner. This article explains what happened, what wildlife experts say about eastern diamondback behaviour, why snake sightings near homes are becoming more common in Southwest Florida, and how to respond if you meet one.How Paul and Brandon Tremblay found an eastern diamondback rattlesnake outside their Gulf Cove homeLawn work was no longer the priority when Charlotte County resident Paul Tremblay and his son Brandon stepped outside and came across a plump eastern diamondback rattlesnake right in front of their Gulf Cove home. The Cool Down, which reported the encounter on 11 October 2026 based on WINK News coverage, says the pair did not expect anything like it. Paul told WINK News they were "genuinely shocked," adding that it is simply not something you expect to see. The family also recorded the encounter and shared the footage with the outlet. Brandon told WINK News that snakes typically don't bother him much, but seeing this one was definitely a little scary. Their reactions will feel familiar to anyone who has ever met a wild animal unexpectedly.What to do when an eastern diamondback rattlesnake shows up near your Florida homeSpotting a rattlesnake near your front door is the kind of surprise that sends a pulse racing, yet what you do next matters far more than the shock itself. In Southwest Florida, the eastern diamondback is a native neighbour, and encounters are becoming more common as communities grow. Knowing who to call, how these snakes behave, and why sightings are increasing can turn a frightening moment into a manageable one. This article walks through a recent encounter, explains what a local naturalist wants residents to understand, and offers practical steps for sharing space with one of the state's misunderstood reptiles.How a Florida father and son safely handled a rattlesnake by calling the sheriff's emergency linePaul and Brandon Tremblay chose not to confront the rattlesnake themselves. Instead, they phoned the county sheriff's emergency line, and officers with the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission removed the animal about 30 minutes later, according to WINK News, as relayed by The Cool Down. The family said the snake was captured safely in roughly half an hour, a fast resolution to what could have been a stressful situation. Brandon Tremblay told WINK News that the rattlesnake was a beautiful animal and a great part of the local ecosystem, showing that relief and respect can go hand in hand.ALSO READ: Nuclear sites fortified, loyalists rallied: Iran braces for possible US attacksWhy eastern diamondback rattlesnake sightings are rising in Florida and how to give wildlife spaceRanger Rob Howell, a naturalist and environmental educator at Pink Shell Resort, told WINK News that the eastern diamondback is one of Florida's five venomous snakes, yet it is not looking for confrontations with people. He explained that the snake would bite only if it believed you were its food or a threat, so his advice is simple: give it space and leave it alone. Howell also told WINK News that development is contributing to more frequent sightings, and that changing weather can send these snakes searching for shelter from the cold. articles.summary: Indian-origin Michigan lawmaker Ranjeev Puri is hoping to make history by becoming the first Indian-American to serve as Speaker of a state House in the
articles.body: Indian-origin Michigan lawmaker Ranjeev Puri is hoping to make history by becoming the first Indian-American to serve as Speaker of a state House in the United States. His prospects depend on whether Democrats can wrest control of the Michigan House of Representatives from Republicans in the November 3 elections.Puri, 42, currently serves as the Democratic leader in the Michigan House, where Republicans hold the majority. Republican Speaker Matt Hall leads the 110-member chamber, while Michigan has a Democratic governor, Gretchen Whitmer.US Congresswoman Haley Stevens recently expressed confidence that Democrats could flip the chamber and elevate Puri to the top post.“Michigan Dems are on the move. We are about to flip the state house and make Ranjeev Puri THE FIRST Indian American State House Speaker in the country,” Stevens said while campaigning for Democrats.Puri is also seeking another term in the state legislature and faces Republican candidate Allison Kay Fuller in his election contest.Who is Ranjeev Puri?Born around 1984 in Racine, Wisconsin, Puri is the son of Punjabi immigrants from India. He became the first Sikh-American elected to the Michigan House of Representatives in 2020, taking office in January 2021.Before entering electoral politics, Puri worked on former US President Barack Obama's presidential campaigns in 2008 and 2012. His experience in the campaigns helped shape his interest in public service and community engagement.Puri earned a bachelor's degree in economics and finance from Ohio State University before completing an MBA at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business in 2014. He also worked in business development for Fiat Chrysler before entering the Michigan legislature.Since being elected, Puri has risen through the Democratic Party's ranks. He served as a Democratic whip before becoming the party's leader in the Republican-controlled House in January 2025.His legislative work has included issues such as gun safety, infrastructure and economic development. He has also been involved in transportation budget discussions in Michigan, a state with a major automotive industry.According to the Indian American Voter Atlas, Michigan is home to around 127,000 people of Indian origin, accounting for approximately 1.27% of its population.The November 3 elections will determine whether Puri secures another term and whether Democrats win the majority needed to put him in contention for the speakership.If successful, his elevation would mark a milestone for Indian-American representation in state-level politics across the US.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2024, a New York charity began raising money for free retreats for disabled veterans; two years later, the state alleged nearly $100,000 in donations helped fund insiders' property and personal expenses
articles.summary: A New York veterans' charity created to offer outdoor retreats for injured service members became a personal source of money for its leaders, state
articles.body: A New York veterans' charity created to offer outdoor retreats for injured service members became a personal source of money for its leaders, state prosecutors allege in a civil lawsuit. The lawsuit filed by the Office of the New York Attorney General claims that Healing for Heroes, A Disabled Veteran's Retreat and Wooded Oasis, Inc., misled local community groups, businesses, and donors. According to the lawsuit, the charity used their donations to pay for personal luxuries and improvements for its founders instead of helping former service members. According to legal filings submitted by the Office of the New York Attorney General, the charity raised nearly $100,000 in donations after launching in 2024. Investigators say almost half of that money went toward personal shopping trips, restaurant meals, vehicle repairs, fuel, and improvements to property owned by the charity's leaders. State officials are asking the court to shut down the organisation, ban its founders from running non-profits in New York, and order them to return the misused money and pay civil penalties.Private stays and turned-away applicantsThe charity operated from a 30-acre wooded property in Bemus Point, Chautauqua County. Its official promotional materials said the land would offer a free, peaceful place for wounded former service members to rest and recover. Investigators from the Office of the New York Attorney General found that the non-profit held just four retreats in 2024 and 2025. All four events were attended only by board members, their relatives, and close personal friends. This meant donated money was effectively used to pay for private family holidays. When disabled veterans with no personal ties to the charity's leaders asked about booking stays, the organisation turned them away before they could even apply. Court documents say the charity's leaders later claimed they could not afford to host full weekend retreats. Instead of offering stays lasting several days, the organisation held short gatherings with food donated by local businesses. These events included activities called "Free Pizza & Fire Night" and "Coffee and Donuts." Each gathering lasted only a few hours and cost the organisation almost nothing.Unreported income and personal accountsAlong with collecting donations, Board President Thomas Nelsen and Board Secretary and Treasurer Jennifer Milchanoski-Nelsen rented out the 30-acre property in Bemus Point through Airbnb at least 32 times in 2024 and 2025. Their rental listings told holidaymakers that all the money earned would support disabled veterans. However, state investigators found that the couple kept all $33,312.16 earned from these rentals. The payments went directly into their personal bank account. The Office of the New York Attorney General found that the non-profit started collecting money from the public in 2024 before registering as a charity in New York state. The organisation also operated without an effective board of directors or a formal policy to manage conflicts of interest. Financial checks showed that cash donations and payments through Venmo went into personal accounts instead of accounts held by the organisation. The leaders also failed to record donated work, professional services, and valuable equipment given by supporters. These items included several all-terrain vehicles and an SUV.Misleading promises to donorsThe charity's fundraising campaigns promised that 100 percent of public donations would pay for therapeutic retreats for former military personnel. Instead, court records show that donations paid for a new wooden deck and a complete bathroom renovation at the Nelsen home. "Our veterans have sacrificed so much for this country, and they deserve real supportive services when they return to civilian life," Attorney General Letitia James said in a statement released by her office. "Healing for Heroes exploited veterans' service and betrayed the trust of their donors, including local community members, veterans' organizations, and businesses to enrich themselves and their friends. My office has no tolerance for charities that use noble causes to scam New Yorkers out of their hard-earned money."Demands for dissolution and financial penaltiesThe civil lawsuit filed by the Office of the New York Attorney General accuses the organisation and its officers of breaking state charity laws, using deceptive business practices, making false advertising claims, and failing to keep basic financial records. Prosecutors want the court to shut down the organisation permanently and transfer its remaining assets to legitimate non-profit groups that help disabled veterans. The lawsuit also asks the court to permanently ban Thomas Nelsen and Jennifer Milchanoski-Nelsen from collecting charitable donations or serving as officers or directors of any non-profit registered in New York state. The state is seeking full repayment of the money taken from donors, along with fines set by law. Legal filings request penalties of $1,000 for each violation of New York charities law and up to $5,000 for each violation of the state's FAIR Business Practices Act. Assistant Attorney General Paulette Campbell is leading the case through the state regional office in Buffalo.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Don’t post videos, stay indoors': Embassy issues fresh advisory for Indians in Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian embassies in Saudi Arabia on Tuesday issued fresh advisories for Indian nationals amid flight disruptions following the suspension of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian embassies in Saudi Arabia on Tuesday issued fresh advisories for Indian nationals amid flight disruptions following the suspension of services by Indian airlines to several Saudi cities until October 17.The Indian Embassy in Riyadh advised Indian nationals to remain calm and vigilant, stay indoors in the event of an aerial attack and follow instructions issued by local authorities through official channels. It also urged Indians to refrain from circulating or reposting videos or news related to the ongoing events.The Embassy said Air India and Air India Express had suspended flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until October 17. Akasa Air suspended services to and from Riyadh and Jeddah, while IndiGo cancelled flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah and Medina until the same date.The General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) has announced the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Operations at other major airports, including Dammam, Jeddah and Medina, are continuing, although disruptions have been reported.The Embassy advised Indian nationals to remain in regular contact with their respective airlines and verify the latest status of their flights. Those needing to leave Saudi Arabia in an emergency may also consider flights from neighbouring Gulf countries, particularly Qatar and Bahrain, subject to obtaining the required visas.The Consulate General of India in Jeddah issued a separate advisory, particularly for Umrah pilgrims travelling to and from Jeddah and Medina. It urged passengers to check with airlines before proceeding to airports and remain in contact with travel agents, tour operators and Umrah service providers regarding cancellations, rescheduling, alternative travel arrangements and accommodation.The Consulate said it was in regular contact with airlines and local authorities to assist affected Indian nationals. Both the Embassy in Riyadh and the Consulate in Jeddah have established 24x7 control rooms to provide assistance.The Riyadh Embassy also said Indian nationals who arrived in Saudi Arabia on visit, tourist, Umrah or business visas but were forced to overstay because of flight unavailability would be allowed to leave without paying fines. Those whose visas have expired were advised to exit the Kingdom as soon as flights become available.ALSO READ: Flydubai mid-air stabbing: 2 Maldivian pilots detained in UAE over links with accused Omani copilot - reportIndian national killed in Riyadh airport attackThe fresh advisories come after an October 10 attack on Riyadh airport killed Indian national Mohammed Yousef Ali. Ambassador Vipul and Embassy officials attended his funeral in Riyadh on October 12, in accordance with his family's wishes, and assured the bereaved family of continued support.The Embassy said four Indian nationals injured in the attack remained in intensive care, four were receiving treatment in normal wards and three had been discharged. Officials were visiting hospitals and maintaining contact with the injured and their families.Meanwhile, IndiGo, Akasa Air and Air India announced the extended suspension of their services, citing the evolving security situation and risks to safe flight operations. Air India and Akasa Air said affected passengers could seek full refunds, while Akasa Air also offered rescheduling without additional charges.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A shopper paid just £15 for an old ring in a Leicester charity shop, then experts traced it to the British royal family; the rare Princess Amelia mourning ring later sold at auction for £5,500
articles.summary: A shopper who paid £15 for an old ring at a charity shop in Leicester has made thousands of pounds after auction experts linked the item to the British
articles.body: A shopper who paid £15 for an old ring at a charity shop in Leicester has made thousands of pounds after auction experts linked the item to the British royal family. The rare ring turned out to be a 19th-century gold and enamel mourning ring made to mark the death of Princess Amelia, the youngest daughter of King George III and Queen Charlotte. It was sold at Hansons Auctioneers in Etwall, Derbyshire, where intense bidding from buyers around the world pushed the final price to £5,500. According to Hansons Auctioneers, the buyer spotted the ring among everyday items in a local charity shop without knowing its historical importance. After taking it to experts for an appraisal, specialists identified the detailed gold ring as a rare item from the Regency era.Hidden high street treasureCharles Hanson, owner and director of Hansons Auctioneers, described the item as "the most important charity shop find I've heard about in a decade." Details shared by Hansons Auctioneers show that when the owner brought the ring in for a valuation, specialists recognised features linked to royal jewellery made during the reign of King George III. "I was stunned and dazzled," Mr Hanson said in an official announcement published by the auction house. "From a simple box emerged a piece of deeply personal Royal history, commissioned by the Royal family itself to honour a lost loved one. This mourning ring was created to commemorate the life and death of Princess Amelia, and it speaks volumes in its craftsmanship and symbolism."Poignant piece of royal historyPrincess Amelia was born on 7 August 1783 and was the youngest of the 15 children of King George III and Queen Charlotte. She was widely reported to be her father's favourite daughter. She died on 2 November 1810, aged 27, after a long battle with tuberculosis. Historical records cited by Hansons Auctioneers state that her death deeply affected the King and played a major role in his final and lasting decline in mental health. According to accounts of her final hours, Princess Amelia pressed a ring containing a lock of her hair into her father's hand as she lay dying. She is said to have whispered the words "remember me". After her funeral at Windsor, her elder brother, the Prince Regent, who later became King George IV, asked court goldsmiths Rundell, Bridge & Rundell to make 52 mourning rings. These were made in her memory and given only to close family members and trusted friends of the royal household. The ring has a crown design above the initial 'A'. It also carries the words "Remember me" in white enamel. "The white enamel used in the ring denotes that Amelia was unmarried at the time of her death," Mr Hanson explained. "White enamel symbolised purity and innocence in mourning jewellery, particularly for those who died young or unmarried. It contrasts with the more commonly used black enamel, which signified general mourning."International interest at auctionWhen the royal goldsmiths Rundell, Bridge & Rundell made the 52 mourning rings in 1810, each one cost 58 shillings, according to the original invoice. Interest in these royal memorial items has continued over the centuries. Records held by Hansons Auctioneers show that Queen Mary bought an identical mourning ring for the Royal Collection in 1935. Before the June Fine Art, Silver, Jewellery & Watches Auction at Hansons' Derbyshire auction house, experts estimated that the ring would sell for between £3,000 and £4,000. "This find proves treasures still lie hidden on our high streets," Mr Hanson said before the sale. "It's not just the monetary value, it's the emotion, history and humanity behind this ring that truly moves you."Surpassing estimate under the hammerOn auction day, buyers bidding by telephone, online and in the auction room competed for the ring, listed as Lot 63 in the catalogue. Daniel Armstrong, fine art auction lead at Hansons Auctioneers, oversaw the sale as bids rose above the original estimate. The ring eventually sold for £5,500. This gave the buyer a return of more than 360 times the £15 paid at the charity shop. "This sale was a perfect marriage of beauty, history and market energy," Mr Armstrong said in a post-auction report published by Hansons Auctioneers. "From ancient craftsmanship to royal remembrance, we were privileged to handle pieces that resonate deeply with collectors. Bidders were competing with purpose and passion, it was a joy to watch." The sale was part of a successful group of lots at the Derbyshire auction house. Other items included an Ancient Greek chalcedony ring, which sold for £5,600, and a Regency partner's desk, which raised £38,000 for charity.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: The great Indian scam trap: More aware, yet still vulnerable
articles.summary: A recent report highlights the increasing awareness of online scams among Indian consumers, yet alarming statistics reveal their continued vulnerability to fraud. Discover the key findings from the GSMA India Consumer Scam Report 2026 and learn how online shopping, messaging apps, and psychological tactics put many at risk.
articles.body: A 79-year-old woman in Mumbai recently tried to buy dry fruits worth Rs 248 after seeing an advertisement on WhatsApp. Instead, she lost Rs 11.7 lakh after a caller posing as a company representative persuaded her to make 13 UPI transfers. She was warned that her bank account could be closed due to a technical error.Her experience brings together several findings in the GSMA India Consumer Scam Report 2026, based on an online, English-language survey of about 500 Indian adults conducted from July 29 to August 3. Online shopping scams were cited by 33% of Indian victims, more than any other type. Among surveyed victims who lost money, two in three recovered nothing.The survey compares Indian respondents with those in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam. Three in four Indians surveyed (75%) said they were very concerned about online data privacy, against 48% across those six countries. Yet two in three (66%) were comfortable sharing personal details with “conversational apps” when buying, against 40% across the region. A third (33%) said they were "very comfortable" doing so, against just 7%. The report does not name the apps or establish whether respondents actually shared their details.Trusting the channels scammers useIndians also rate everyday communication channels as more trustworthy than respondents in the six Southeast Asian countries. These are also channels regularly used by scammers. Among Indian victims, 42% were scammed through messaging apps, 37% through social media and 33% through email. The email figure is almost double the regional 17%. And 64% of Indian victims were scammed through multiple channels, against 43% across the Southeast Asian countries.After online shopping, prize, lottery or inheritance scams were cited by 31% of Indian victims (remember the Nigerian prince emails?), and job or income scams by 30%. QR-code or payment-link scams were cited by 27%, against 18% across the region.Scammers also apply psychological pressure. Urgency featured in 39% of Indian victims' experiences, while secrecy or confidentiality featured in 33%, against a regional average of 22% for secrecy. In the Mumbai case, the alleged fraudster created a fear of losing banking access by warning that a technical problem could lead to account closure. Digital-arrest scams often play on the secrecy angle by leveraging potentially sensitive information.Technology adds another layer. Nearly half of Indian respondents (48%) said they had encountered AI-written scam messages, the same share reported fake AI images, and 42% said they had seen deepfake videos of real people.The changing behaviour patternIndians are gradually becoming more guarded against scams. Seventy-two per cent of Indian respondents said their own experience, or that of someone close to them, had changed how they behave. Sixty-one per cent avoided some incoming contacts or online transactions because of scam concerns, and 26% had cut back on or changed how they shop online, up from 20% in 2025.There is healthy scepticism about platforms too. Sixty per cent associated Facebook with scams, up from 51% in 2025, and Instagram's figure rose from 50% to 57%.But only 49% had strengthened their account security, against 58% across the region. Among victims, 93% said that, in hindsight, they had done something they should not have, and 91% felt confident they would not fall for a similar scam again.Indians are relatively willing to let institutions use their data to detect fraud. Of the respondents, 87% were comfortable with banks or financial providers doing so, 82% with the government, 81% with mobile operators and 73% with digital platforms, each higher than the corresponding regional figure.Recovering losses is difficultTwelve per cent of Indian respondents said they had been scammed in the previous year, against 8% across the region. Of the 165 Indian respondents who had ever been scammed, 86% approached at least one organisation, against 69% across the region. The share going to the police rose from 37% in the 2025 survey to 49%.However, a third of reported cases remained unresolved, and in 35%, no organisation took primary responsibility in the victim's experience. Among those who lost money, 67% recovered nothing. India's recovery outcome was nevertheless better than the six-country average. Some 33% recovered some or all of their money, against 18% across the region.The home ministry told Parliament that the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System had "saved" more than Rs 11,158 crore across over 32.80 lakh complaints by June 30, 2026, but that figure does not show how much victims got back. In a separate disclosure, the ministry reported more than Rs 206 crore refunded over the three financial years from 2023-24 to 2025-26. The National Crime Records Bureau does not maintain data on money lost or recovered in cyber fraud cases, Rajya Sabha was informed.Scam, a global menace GSMA, which represents mobile operators, calls for closer coordination among banks, platforms, telecom companies and authorities after scams are reported, and for greater transparency from government and police.Scams are a global business. The Global Anti-Scam Alliance estimates that consumers across 42 surveyed markets lost about $442 billion to scams in a year. In the US, the FBI recorded $20.877 billion in cybercrime losses in 2025, more than $2.9 billion of it from two forms of call-centre fraud: fake tech support and government impersonation. The FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report recorded 5,879 complaints from India, the second-highest among countries outside the US, after Canada.Since 2022, the FBI and CBI have run 27 joint operations against such fraud in India, leading to more than 475 arrests. One of them, Operation Chakra, broke up a Noida-based network in December 2025 accused of duping more than 600 Americans of over $48.7 million.If you are conned, call 1930 immediately. articles.title: L Murugan writes to PM Modi seeking exit from Union Cabinet, says wants to return to grassroots
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union minister of state for Information and Broadcasting L Murugan has sought to step down from the Union Council of Ministers and relinquish
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union minister of state for Information and Broadcasting L Murugan has sought to step down from the Union Council of Ministers and relinquish his Rajya Sabha membership, saying he wants to return to grassroots politics.Murugan said he intends to devote himself full-time to strengthening the BJP in Tamil Nadu and preparing the party for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.In a letter addressed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Murugan said he wished to focus on expanding the party’s presence across the state. He also shared the letter on X, reiterating his commitment to working with party workers.“With humility and a grateful heart, I therefore request you to relieve me of my responsibilities as Minister of State and permit me to relinquish my membership of the Rajya Sabha, so that I may dedicate myself full-time to strengthening the party in Tamil Nadu,” Murugan wrote in the letter.He added, “I want to go to every village and every street, meet our people, stand beside our karyakartas and help expand the party's presence in every part of the State.”In his post on X, Murugan said, “It has been the greatest honour of my life to serve Bharat Mata and Tamil Nadu under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi.”“Now, I wish to return to the grassroots, stand with our karyakartas and dedicate myself full-time to strengthening the BJP in Tamil Nadu ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections,” he added.Murugan also expressed gratitude to Modi for giving him the opportunity to serve in the Union government, highlighting his background as the son of daily wage labourers.“I do not come from a political family. I come from a very poor family. My parents, who worked as daily wage labourers and cattle grazers, continue to lead a simple life in Konur village,” he wrote.Reflecting on his political journey, Murugan said his guiding principle over nearly three decades in the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and the BJP had remained: “Nation First, Party Next, Self Last.”Murugan has served as minister of state for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs. From July 2021 to June 2024, he also held the portfolios of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying alongside Information and Broadcasting. He previously served as vice-chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes from 2017 to 2020 and as BJP Tamil Nadu president.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Japanese farmer spent decades planting thousands of pink flowers after his wife went blind due to diabetes; this is why he wanted visitors to come to their home
articles.summary: When Yasuko Kuroki lost her eyesight, the life she and her husband, Toshiyuki Kuroki, had planned together changed.
articles.body: When Yasuko Kuroki lost her eyesight, the life she and her husband, Toshiyuki Kuroki, had planned together changed. The Japanese couple had spent decades working on their dairy farm in Miyazaki Prefecture, raising their family and looking forward to travelling around Japan after retirement. But complications from diabetes left Yasuko blind, and she gradually withdrew from the outside world. Her husband wanted to find a way to help her reconnect with people. His idea was to plant thousands of pink flowers around their home, creating a garden that would attract visitors and give his wife more opportunities to spend time with others.As reported by the UK media portal Daily Mail, Toshiyuki transformed their property in Shintomi Town into a landscape filled with pink ‘shibazakura’ flowers, also known as moss phlox, after noticing that people passing by stopped to admire the blooms.Yasuko Kuroki lost her eyesight after 30 years of marriageAccording to the Daily Mail, Toshiyuki and Yasuko had been married for 30 years when she began experiencing problems with her sight. Within a week, she had lost her eyesight following complications related to diabetes. The couple had built their lives around their dairy farm, where they woke early every morning to look after a herd of 60 cows. Their plans for retirement included travelling around Japan, but Yasuko's sudden loss of sight changed those plans. Yasuko became deeply withdrawn after losing her eyesight. She stayed inside the house and avoided meeting people, while Toshiyuki watched her struggle to adjust to the change in her life. Yasuko became isolated after losing her sight. Toshiyuki wanted to find something that would encourage her to go outside and reconnect with the world around her.Why Toshiyuki Kuroki began planting thousands of pink flowersThe idea came from a small garden that already existed on their property. Toshiyuki noticed people stopping to admire the bright pink shibazakura flowers, also called moss phlox. He began thinking about what might happen if he planted many more of them. If the garden attracted more visitors, they might come to the couple's home, talk to Yasuko and offer her company. According to the Daily Mail, Toshiyuki gave up dairy farming and devoted his time to developing the garden. The report said he spent two years preparing the ground, cutting down trees and caring for the young plants before the landscape began to take shape.That initial work was only the beginning. An archived Japanese gardening record indicates that Toshiyuki continued developing the garden over more than two decades. By 2016, the property covered around 4,000 square metres. The flowers were chosen for more than their appearance. Their fragrance was also important. Although Yasuko could no longer see the pink blooms, she could still experience their scent. As reported by Good News Network, the garden helped encourage Yasuko to spend time outside. As visitors began arriving, she had more opportunities to talk to people instead of remaining isolated inside the house.The garden attracted visitors during the flowering seasonOver the years, the garden around the Kuroki home developed into a large carpet of pink flowers. The blooms were at their fullest during March and April, drawing visitors to Shintomi Town in Miyazaki Prefecture. As reported by The Daily Mail, the site had more than 7,000 visitors a year. The garden became known for more than its flowers. Visitors were also interested in the story behind it: a husband who had spent years transforming his property because he wanted his wife to have more company.According to the Daily Mail, visitors could also see the couple's old cow sheds and learn about the garden's history. The property, once centred on dairy farming, had become a place where people came to see the blooms and learn why they had been planted.What happened to the Kuroki flower garden?The garden's story continued after it attracted international attention, but its organised public opening did not continue indefinitely. The garden's run as a public attraction came to an end in 2017, after around three decades of maintenance by Toshiyuki Kuroki. According to a Japanese gardening record documenting the garden's history, Kuroki decided to end its general public opening in cooperation with Shintomi Town because maintaining the garden had become physically demanding as he grew older. A report published by the local Miyazaki Nichinichi Shimbun on April 13, 2017, also noted that the season would be the last for the famous hillside of pink shibazakura.You use AI every day.
