articles.title: ‘I never imagined I’d end up in this situation’:  IIT Kanpur alumnus, 61, struggles to find a US tech job for nearly two years, turns to gig work and considers…
articles.summary: For more than two decades, Gautam Dev built his career in the US technology industry, expecting his experience to help him navigate the ups and downs of
articles.body: For more than two decades, Gautam Dev built his career in the US technology industry, expecting his experience to help him navigate the ups and downs of the job market. But at 61, the IIT Kanpur alumnus finds himself struggling to secure a full-time position, pay rent and manage mounting bills. Now, he is considering returning to India, where he lived before moving to the US more than two decades ago.Dev shared his experience in an as-told-to essay published by Business Insider. His difficulties began in September 2024, when his employer told him he would have to relocate to another state to keep his software engineering job. Rather than move, he decided to leave the job and look for another opportunity while staying in Dallas, Texas.What he expected to be a temporary gap between jobs has turned into a prolonged struggle. Despite years of experience, applications and interviews, he has yet to secure another full-time role. “In 2024, while working as a software engineer for an IT company in Dallas, I was told I'd have to relocate to another state to keep my job. That September, I decided to quit my job, stay in Dallas, and look for a new role. That decision became a disaster,” Dev told Business Insider. His account has also been reported by Indian media outlets.When experience did not translate into a new jobDev said he had faced employment gaps earlier in his career, but they had usually lasted only a few months before he found another position. This time, the search has been markedly different. He initially looked for vacancies, primarily through LinkedIn, and contacted people in his professional network. However, many told him their companies were not hiring. Some said their jobs had become more demanding but that they were reluctant to leave because they feared they might struggle to find another position.Dev did manage to secure interviews, including multiple rounds with the same company. Yet none led to a job offer. “I didn’t realise how difficult finding another job would be,” he said. He believes several factors may be affecting his prospects, including his age, the length of his employment gap and changes in the technology industry. Dev said he had come across openings in artificial intelligence engineering but did not feel confident applying for roles that required experience he lacked. His account does not establish why individual employers rejected his applications. However, it reflects the uncertainty he has experienced while trying to return to full-time employment after decades in the industry.From software engineering to gig workAfter months of applications and unsuccessful interviews, Dev decided to spend less time actively searching for full-time work and more time trying to earn money. “I need to spend that time earning money instead,” he said. He tried day trading, which initially went well before his fortunes changed. He also turned to gig work through platforms such as Uber, DoorDash and Walmart Spark. The work has provided some income, but not enough to cover his expenses comfortably.Dev said his physical limitations also restrict the kind of delivery work he can take on, as he cannot carry heavy items. With his earnings falling short, his financial position has become increasingly difficult. He has drawn down his savings and accumulated credit card debt while trying to keep up with rent and other bills. “Even with gig work, it's become difficult to keep paying the bills. I've had to drain my savings and take on a lot of credit card debt,” he said.Finding cheaper accommodation has also proved difficult to navigate. Dev would like to move to a less expensive place in Dallas but worries that a landlord could ask for proof of employment and a steady income. Moving would also take time away from delivery work, affecting the money he can earn.A fundraiser, Social Security and the possibility of returning to IndiaIn January, Dev started a GoFundMe fundraiser to help pay his bills. According to his account, it raised more than $9,000, which went towards his expenses. “It was hard to ask people for money, and not everyone has been supportive. But some people have been really nice and generous,” he said. He is now looking towards another potential source of income. Dev expects to become eligible for Social Security benefits when he turns 62 in January 2027. He hopes the payments, combined with whatever he can earn through gig work, will ease some of the financial pressure.Returning to India is also under consideration. Dev lived in India before moving to the US more than two decades ago and eventually becoming an American citizen. However, he has said he is not rushing into a decision, as relocating would require time and careful planning. For now, he intends to continue gig work while weighing his options. The prospect of leaving the US after building a career there marks a difficult turning point for someone who had expected his professional experience to provide greater security. “I never imagined I’d end up in this situation, but here I am,” he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Maine was replacing an aging river bridge when part of the new structure collapsed during a concrete pour and injured workers; two months later, crews are dismantling the damaged spans before construction resumes
articles.summary: Demolition crews in Maine have started removing damaged parts of a new river bridge that partly collapsed while workers were pouring concrete.
articles.body: Demolition crews in Maine have started removing damaged parts of a new river bridge that partly collapsed while workers were pouring concrete. The incident sent injured workers to hospital and brought a major bridge replacement project to a halt. Engineers and heavy equipment operators are cutting apart and removing damaged sections of the new Llewellyn Estes Bridge over the Stillwater River in Old Town. According to updates published by the Maine Department of Transportation (MaineDOT), contractors are using special heavy machinery to separate damaged sections from the supporting piers and abutments. They are then lifting the broken pieces out of the river. The demolition follows an incident on August 13, when a newly built section of the bridge suddenly failed as workers poured wet concrete for the new bridge deck.Controlled dismantling and river cleanupDemolition work began on Tuesday, 13 October. Crews must break the collapsed structure into smaller pieces while working above the water. Officials at MaineDOT confirmed that heavy equipment operators are carefully lifting the broken materials out of the Stillwater River. The debris will then be taken to dry land for processing and disposal. Engineers planned the slow, careful removal process to protect workers and avoid damaging nearby concrete piers and abutments that survived the original collapse. To make room for the large cranes and equipment needed for the work, state transport officials introduced daytime traffic closures on the nearby temporary bridge carrying Stillwater Avenue. Under guidelines issued by MaineDOT, the temporary bridge will close at intervals between 9 am and 3 pm. Transport officials have set up a signed detour directing drivers along Bennoch Road, North Main Street, and College Avenue while heavy lifting takes place above the road. Safety teams said the need for road closures would decrease as demolition work moved downstream and farther away from the active detour lane.Collapse during concrete deck pourThe incident happened on 13 August 2026 during construction of a modern replacement for the ageing Llewellyn Estes Bridge. The bridge carries Stillwater Avenue over two channels of the Stillwater River. As workers poured wet concrete onto the bridge deck, one of the main spans suddenly failed and collapsed into the river below. Several construction workers were injured in the fall and needed immediate medical checks and treatment. The new bridge was still under construction and closed to public traffic when the collapse happened. Drivers were already using a nearby temporary bridge built by MaineDOT to keep traffic moving through Old Town. After the accident, state inspectors examined the temporary bridge to check whether the collapse of the nearby structure had affected its safety. The inspection confirmed that the temporary bridge remained stable and safe for public use.Multi-agency forensic investigationState transport officials launched a detailed investigation to find out what caused the bridge deck to fail. MaineDOT partnered with the Federal Highway Administration's Turner-Fairbank Highway Research Center to carry out the investigation and provide independent structural analysis and technical support. The review team also includes the main contractor, Reed & Reed, Inc., the beam designer and manufacturer, Basalt Engineering International, and the Advanced Structures and Composites Center. Investigation teams inspected the site and collected material samples from the debris. They are reviewing design calculations, records of how materials were made, and the procedures used to pour the concrete. In an official statement released after the incident, MaineDOT officials stressed that a full investigation was needed before construction could safely restart. "MaineDOT and its partners continue to collect and review all available information and data related to the design, fabrication, and construction of the new Llewellyn Estes Bridge," the department said in an official public statement. "This information gathering is part of a thorough and comprehensive review to determine the factors that led to the failure of one of the new spans during concrete placement of the new bridge deck."Next steps for bridge replacementThe Llewellyn Estes Bridge replacement is part of Maine's wider infrastructure improvement programme. The programme aims to replace ageing river crossings across Penobscot County. Once demolition crews finish removing the damaged concrete and support beams from the Stillwater River, engineers will examine the exposed foundation piers to assess their condition. Plans to rebuild the bridge will depend on the findings of the joint investigation led by MaineDOT and federal highway investigators. State transport officials said public safety remains the main priority. They will provide further traffic updates and details about the project schedule as the cleanup work progresses.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'His blood splattered over everybody': US man dies after falling from roller coaster ride
articles.summary: A 42-year-old man died after being thrown from a roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia near Atlanta, with witnesses saying he struck other riders
articles.body: A 42-year-old man died after being thrown from a roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia near Atlanta, with witnesses saying he struck other riders before falling to the ground, the Associated Press reported.The deceased was identified as Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, an Atlanta resident, by Cobb County police. According to news agency AP, authorities said multiple people were injured but did not provide details about their injuries or conditions. The department's Major Crimes Unit is investigating the incident.Witnesses told local media that the incident occurred on Goliath, a roller coaster that reaches speeds of around 70 mph and rises to a height of about 200 feet. The ride was temporarily halted following the incident, with passengers seen being evacuated and walking down a steep incline.‘His blood splattered over everybody’: Witnesses recount horrorA woman who was at the park told Atlanta-based news outlet 11Alive that she saw the man fall from the ride and hit another passenger."A man fell off the Goliath ride," she said, adding that he struck a girl sitting two rows ahead of her near the point where photographs are taken during the ride.She said the man hit the roller coaster car several times before falling. "His blood splattered over everybody, and his body fell behind one of the haunted attractions," she told 11Alive.The woman said passengers were made to wait for some time before they were allowed to exit the ride.Another witness, Logan Conner, who was riding Goliath with his fiancée, described seeing the man come out of his seat."The man started levitating in the air sideways," he told NBC. "We made direct eye contact with him."Another couple who witnessed the incident said the roller coaster struck the man several times before he was thrown from the ride."It went from having a great time to just screaming, 'Oh my God, what is happening,'" the woman said, describing the sudden shift from excitement to panic.Nine similar roller coasters shut as precautionSix Flags Entertainment Corp. temporarily shut nine similar roller coasters across six amusement parks in North America following the incident, citing an abundance of caution.The rides include Raging Bull at Six Flags Great America, Goliath at Six Flags Magic Mountain, Nitro at Six Flags Great Adventure, Leviathan and Behemoth at Canada's Wonderland, Fury 325 and Thunder Striker at Carowinds, and Orion and Diamondback at Kings Island.A company spokesperson said park staff and local authorities responded immediately and that the company was cooperating with the investigation."We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today," the spokesperson said, adding that support was being provided to affected visitors and employees.The park was already scheduled to be closed on Tuesday. Six Flags has not announced when the temporarily suspended rides will reopen.Goliath, which opened in 2006, features a drop of more than 200 feet and reaches speeds of around 70 mph, according to the park's website.Death follows safety concerns over another Six Flags rideThe fatal incident comes less than two weeks after Six Flags Magic Mountain in California announced the permanent retirement of its X2 roller coaster following lawsuits alleging that riders had suffered serious brain injuries.The ride, which features rotating seats, a 215-foot drop and multiple flips, had been closed since July 12. One lawsuit involved a rider who allegedly suffered a catastrophic brain injury, while the park also settled a wrongful-death lawsuit involving a 22-year-old man who died after riding X2 in 2022.The latest incident has prompted fresh scrutiny of roller coaster safety as authorities investigate what caused Kariem to fall from the Goliath ride.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Bihar Governor Syed Ata Hasnain urges expansion of Lok Bhavan faculty development programme to all universities and colleges to boost teaching quality and standards.
articles.body: Patna: Governor-cum-chancellor Syed Ata Hasnain has called for expanding Lok Bhavan’s faculty development programme to every university and college in the state, while directing officials to make its subsequent phases more effective.Reviewing the first phase on Tuesday, Governor expressed satisfaction with the positive feedback but stressed that the initiative must translate into tangible improvements in teaching quality and academic standards.Launched on Sept 27, the programme’s first phase concludes on Wednesday. It has exposed teachers across state universities and constituent colleges to emerging and critical subjects, including artificial intelligence (AI), information and communication technology (ICT), research, Indian knowledge tradition, sustainable development goals, economy and environment.The initiative seeks to strengthen teachers’ professional competence, encourage innovation in classroom teaching and create a better academic environment for students. Eminent academicians from national and state-level institutions have guided the participants.The programme has been implemented with significant contributions from UGC Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Centres at Patna University and Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University, Muzaffarpur, IIT-Patna and Central University of South Bihar, Gaya. Governor’s adviser Binod Kumar Tripathi coordinated the initiative.Hasnain commended the participating institutions, academicians and officials for the programme’s successful execution. articles.title: CNG shortage hits Erode, Namakkal districts; fuel stations see long queues of vehicles

articles.body: NAMAKKAL: A severe shortage of compressed natural gas (CNG) in Erode and Namakkal districts has caused hardship for motorists and taxi operators, forcing many to spend hours waiting for fuel.More than 100 cars and several Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (TNSTC) buses were seen queued up outside a few private CNG filling stations at Vediyarasampalayam and Pallipalayam in Namakkal district on Tuesday.Drivers said the shortage had persisted for the past few days in Erode and surrounding areas, severely affecting their livelihood. Call taxi operators complained that they were unable to accept bookings regularly. “We were spending considerable time travelling from one fuel station to another in search of CNG,” said S Palanivel, a taxi driver.They said even when gas was available at select outlets, priority was given to govt transport vehicles, resulting in long waiting times for private vehicles and taxi operators.Vehicle owners and taxi drivers urged the authorities concerned and oil companies to take immediate steps to restore regular CNG supplies and address the ongoing shortage.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Coimbatore | Silver Rate in Coimbatore | Bank Holidays in Coimbatore | Public Holidays in Coimbatore | Coimbatore AQI | Weather in Coimbatore | Petrol Price in Coimbatore | Diesel Price in Coimbatore | CNG Price in Coimbatore | LPG Price in CoimbatoreStay updated with the latest Coimbatore news. articles.title: In 2014, Tony Robbins turned a childhood memory of his struggling family receiving groceries from a stranger into Feeding America’s 100 Million Meals Challenge; expanded later, it reached 1 billion meals in 2023
articles.summary: Tony Robbins’ hunger-relief work began not with a fundraising campaign, but with a memory from his childhood.
articles.body: Tony Robbins’ hunger-relief work began not with a fundraising campaign, but with a memory from his childhood. As the motivational speaker and author has recounted, his family was struggling financially when he was about 11 years old, and a stranger arrived at their home with groceries and a frozen turkey for Thanksgiving. The experience stayed with him and later became part of the inspiration for his partnership with Feeding America, the US-based hunger-relief organisation.In 2014, Robbins and Feeding America launched the 100 Million Meals Challenge, an initiative aimed at helping families facing food insecurity. What began as a campaign to provide millions of meals subsequently expanded into a much larger commitment. In 2017, the partners announced a billion-meal goal, and in November 2023, Feeding America said the challenge had surpassed its target nearly two years ahead of schedule. The organisation has since launched a new initiative to provide another billion meals by 2035.From 100 million meals to a billionThe original challenge was announced on November 21, 2014. According to a Feeding America announcement, Robbins pledged the equivalent of 50 million meals and invited the public to help match his contribution, bringing the campaign’s target to 100 million meals. The contribution included profits from his recently published book, 'Money: Master the Game', along with an additional personal donation. The food was to be distributed through Feeding America’s network of local food banks. The organisation said the campaign built on Robbins’ longstanding support for hunger relief.The initial target was achieved within two years, according to Feeding America’s later account of the partnership. The campaign then grew beyond its original ambition as Robbins and the organisation sought to reach more families experiencing food insecurity.In 2017, the partnership announced an expanded goal of providing one billion meals by the end of 2025. The campaign relied not only on Robbins’ own contributions but also on donations from individuals who responded to his appeals. His approach included matching gifts and directing proceeds from his books towards hunger relief.The expansion reflected the scale of the problem the initiative was trying to address. Feeding America works through a nationwide network of food banks, food pantries and meal programmes to connect people with food. Its model allows contributions to support distribution through local organisations rather than relying on a single central facility.The billion-meal milestone arrived earlyBy September 2022, the partnership had reported that it had helped provide 914 million meals, putting it well on its way to the billion-meal target. At the time, Robbins and Feeding America said the campaign was ahead of schedule despite rising food and transportation costs placing additional pressure on families and hunger-relief organisations.The goal was formally reached in November 2023, nearly two years before the original 2025 deadline. In its announcement dated November 29, 2023, Feeding America credited Robbins and the thousands of donors who joined the effort. The organisation said the initiative had helped provide one billion meals to people facing hunger across the United States.The campaign’s growth also demonstrated how the original pledge had evolved. Robbins had initially sought to help provide 100 million meals, but the partnership subsequently mobilised additional donations and matching contributions to reach a target ten times larger. Feeding America said Robbins increased his personal and business giving over the years, including a further $10 million contribution during the pandemic.The number represents meals the campaign helped provide, rather than a claim that Robbins personally prepared or distributed a billion individual servings. The initiative depended on donations and the infrastructure of Feeding America’s partner network to turn financial contributions into food assistance.A new billion-meal goal by 2035Reaching the target did not end the partnership. In April 2025, Robbins and Feeding America announced the Next Billion Meals Challenge, a fresh 10-year initiative intended to help provide another billion meals to individuals and families experiencing food insecurity by 2035. According to the announcement, the new effort builds on the earlier campaign and includes a lead matching gift from Robbins to encourage further contributions. The campaign had already helped provide more than 50 million meals when the initiative was announced.Feeding America’s campaign page says every $1 donated helps provide at least 10 meals through its network of food banks. The organisation also describes the new initiative as part of a broader effort to address hunger in the US, while Robbins supports other food-recovery organisations, including FarmLink and Sharing Excess.The US-focused campaign is distinct from the wider 100 Billion Meals Challenge, a global initiative Robbins co-founded with David Beasley, the former executive director of the United Nations World Food Programme. The two efforts have different scopes and should not be confused when assessing the reach of the Feeding America partnership.The memory behind the missionRobbins has repeatedly linked his philanthropy to the Thanksgiving visit that he remembers from childhood. In his account, receiving groceries from a stranger showed him how an act of generosity could change a family’s immediate circumstances and leave a lasting impression. That experience has become a central part of how he explains his commitment to hunger relief. Feeding America’s 2015 annual report records his description of growing up in a food-insecure household and says he had partnered with the organisation to provide meals since 2012. The report also highlights his support for the 100 Million Meals Challenge.The campaign’s trajectory, from a 100-million-meal target announced in 2014 to a billion-meal milestone in 2023—shows how the initial pledge developed into a long-running fundraising partnership. Its next phase sets another billion-meal target for 2035, extending an effort Robbins says was shaped by the help his own family received when he was young.You use AI every day. articles.title: In Alberta, Canada built an instrumented road with about 825,000 scrap tyres and waste bottom ash, reportedly saving 103,123 m³ of landfill space
articles.summary: Discover how engineers in Edmonton, Alberta, constructed a revolutionary road using nearly one million scrap tires and waste bottom ash, significantly reducing landfill waste and optimizing frost-resistant pavement conditions.
articles.body: Winters in Edmonton are long and cold, and a road there has to cope with ground that freezes deep and then thaws unevenly in spring. Frozen soil under pavement can heave, and as it thaws, it loses strength, so engineers in cold regions look for ways to keep frost away from the soil that supports a road. Meanwhile, scrap tyres accumulate in large numbers, and burning coal for electricity leaves a residue called bottom ash that has to be put somewhere. Researchers at the University of Alberta set out to test whether both materials could go into a single road. They built one that reports its own condition through sensors embedded in the pavement.How the 2012 test road in Edmonton was built and instrumentedThe Integrated Road Research Facility (IRRF) at the University of Alberta, founded in 2012, describes its test road as unique in Canada. The road links the Edmonton Waste Management Centre with Anthony Henday Drive (Highway 216). The road was built with scrap tyres and waste bottom ash and carries more than 250 geotechnical, environmental and pavement sensors, whose data an automated system sends over the Internet to the university laboratory. The IRRF project description states that more than 8,000 tonnes of recycled tyres, about 825,000 scrap tyres, were processed into tyre-derived aggregate and used to build the road. The same description lists three main research areas: tyre-derived aggregate and tyre-soil mixtures as embankment materials, flexible pavement performance in cold weather, and insulated pavement sections using polystyrene boards, bottom ash and tyre-derived aggregate.Landfill savings of 103,123 m³ reported for the Edmonton test roadThe IRRF reports that building the road diverted these tyres from Edmonton’s landfill and saved approximately 103,123 m³ of landfill space. The first published field results came from Negar Tavafzadeh Haghi and colleagues in Using Field Data to Evaluate Bottom Ash as Pavement Insulation Layer, which appeared in Transportation Research Record in 2014.According to the paper, instrumentation took place at various depths in Edmonton, Alberta, and frost depth, freezing, and thawing duration were evaluated using temperature data from October 2012 to June 2013. From the field data, the authors estimated thermal resistivities (R-values) of 1.4 m²°C/W for bottom ash and 16.7 m²°C/W for polystyrene, and the insulation layers reduced frost depth by at least 28% and 40%, respectively, compared with the control pavement section.Frost depth cut by 24% with bottom ash and 64% with polystyrene in the 2021 studyYunyan Huang and colleagues revisited the road eight years after construction in Performance Evaluation of Different Insulating Materials using Field Temperature and Moisture Data, published in Transportation Research Record in 2021. The study took measurements on three 20 m insulated segments and one control segment. Field temperature and moisture gauges were used to compare the 100 cm bottom ash layer with the 10 cm polystyrene board. It was found that the maximum frost depth for the control segment was 2.10 m, 1.60 m with bottom ash, and 0.75 m with polystyrene insulation, a decrease of 24% and 64%, respectively.You use AI every day. articles.title: Argentina moves to stop first commercial oil project on disputed Falkland Islands, escalating row with UK
articles.summary: Argentina on Tuesday said it has approached an international maritime tribunal seeking to halt an oil development project off the disputed Falkland
articles.body: Argentina on Tuesday said it has approached an international maritime tribunal seeking to halt an oil development project off the disputed Falkland Islands, escalating its dispute with the United Kingdom, which controls the archipelago. According to the office of President Javier Milei, Agrentina has filed a request for provisional measures with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea in Hamburg, Germany, seeking to stop the development of Sea Lion, a $2.2-billion Israeli-British oil project north of the Falkland Islands, to “preserve Argentina’s sovereign rights.”Responding to Argentina's move, the UK accused Buenos Aires of taking “measures beyond its jurisdiction” and engaging in “economic coercion”.“The Sea Lion field lies on the Falkland Islands’ continental shelf. The project is lawful and regulated by the democratically elected Falkland Islands government. Argentina has no jurisdiction over it,” UK Foreign Minister Uma Kumaran told the House of Commons on Tuesday.“Let me be absolutely clear: This government will not stand by while Argentina uses economic coercion against the people of the Falkland Islands. We will do whatever it takes to support them,” Kumaran added.The Sea Lion projectThe Sea Lion project is an offshore oilfield located about 220 kilometres (140 miles) north of the Falkland Islands and will be its first commercial oil venture. After years of delays and disruptions, its developers, Israel's Navitas Petroleum and Britain's Rockhopper Exploration, expect production to begin in 2028.In recent weeks, Milei has intensified Argentina's claim to the Falklands, describing the islands' nascent oil industry as a “threat” to the country's sovereignty and an attempt to “steal” its natural resources.Milei has initiated criminal proceedings against executives and shareholders involved in the Sea Lion project and proposed legislation to strengthen and expand sanctions against companies and suppliers “exploiting” the Falklands' resources without Argentine authorisation. Analysts say Milei is invoking a cause that enjoys broad political support to shore up his popularity as the economy falters ahead of next year's presidential election.Britain, meanwhile, has defended the islanders' right to develop their natural resources and pledged support for companies operating in the territory.The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea is an independent international court established under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea to resolve disputes over maritime rights. Its rulings are legally binding, but the tribunal has no means of enforcing them if a country refuses to comply.The Falklands disputeThe Falkland Islands remain a longstanding national cause in Argentina, where they are known as the Malvinas. Buenos Aires maintains that the UK has “illegally” occupied the islands since 1833, a claim rejected by London, which cites the islanders' wish to remain a British Overseas Territory.In 1982, Argentina's military dictatorship invaded the archipelago in an attempt to seize it from the UK, triggering a 10-week war that ended in Argentina's surrender. The conflict left 649 Argentine troops, 255 British personnel and three islanders dead.After defeating England in the FIFA World Cup semi-final in July, Argentine players displayed a banner reading “Las Malvinas son Argentinas” (“The Falkland Islands are Argentine”), reiterating the country's longstanding claim to the disputed archipelago.(With AP inputs)You use AI every day.
